newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to take anti-steel dumping measures.
newsitem.headline: China says to take anti-steel dumping measures.

text.p: China will this year move to bar the dumping of steel products by foreign countries and cut some imports to help domestic producers keep their grip on the local market, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Beijing would restore port management to curb dumping of ordinary steel products, which in 1996 were sold to China at prices much lower than those on the international market, the official newspaper said.
Trade departments were drafting specific anti-dumping regulations, which had already been submitted for approval by the State Council, or cabinet, it said.

China imported 16 million tonnes of steel in 1996, about 10 million tonnes of which were finished products, and cheaper imports from the former Soviet Union and South Korea had forced a cut in domestic production, it said.
"China will reduce imports of long steel products except for high-grade wire rods this year to ensure domestic producers' hold of the domestic market," it said but gave no details.
Domestic producers should seek to cut prices to become more competitive while boosting quality and service, the newspaper quoted senior researcher Wang Jixiang as saying.
Imported products were not subject to the same taxes as domestic products, meaning domestic manufacturers were not competing on an equal basis with their foreign counterparts, Wang said.
